To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feeding crumble- pellets from 1 to21 days of age improves BW and FCR.
feeding crumblepellets improved the performance of broilers at the end of third week and that an increase of dietary protein (unlike an increase of energy) improved the performance of the broilers.

the crumble-pelllet diet is more effective than the mash diet and that increasing the level of protein in the diet is more effective in increasing the BW and decreasing the FCR of broilers at the end of 3rd week of age than the level of energy in the diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the different forms of diet (crumble-pellet and mash) and the different levels of protein (high and low) and energy (high and low).
the effects of different forms of feed and levels of protein and ME on the performance of broiler chicks at the end of third week.
the effect of form of diets on the performance of broiler chickens at the end 3rd week.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feeding crumble pellets from 1 to the 21st day of age improved BW, feed conversion rate, and the performance of the broiler chickens.
feeding crumble pellets with high protein content from 1 to21 days of age improves BW and FCR.
crumble pellets are better than mash diets for broiler chickens at the end and third week.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the form of diet and protein level should be taken into account when feeding broiler diets at the end of third week.
the use of crumble-pelleted diet with 23% CP and 3200 Kcal/kg ME would be the best diet to feed broiler chickens from 1 to21 days of age.
the form of diet (crumble-pellet vs. mash) had a significant impact on the broiler performance at the end.
The main takeaway from our work is that
broilers fed crumble-pelleted diets from 1 to21 days of age showed better growth performance than mash-fed birds.

the use of crumble-pelleted feed from 1 to21 days of age is recommended for broiler chicks, and that the protein content of the diets should be 23% CP and energy 3000 Kcal/Kg ME for broiler performance at the end.
the form of diet is more important than its composition.
